revision: R1 (2026-08-24): baseline chemistry generation refined - alkalinity is now generated from zone-specific Lee et al. (2006) TA = f(S, T) regional equations (or documented alternatives where Lee et al. does not apply), and the archetype alkalinity ranges are demoted from sampling targets to expected-output plausibility checks
description: Six stylized surface-ocean environment categories used to sample baseline conditions. These are explicitly NOT claimed to reproduce any specific real-world location.

baseline_chemistry_generation.ta0_umol_kg: Calculated from the archetype's mapped empirical relationship (see ta_generation_method per archetype) plus bounded noise - NOT sampled independently, so alkalinity covaries realistically with both salinity and temperature
baseline_chemistry_generation.dic0_umol_kg: Calculated from (TA0, pCO2_0, T, S) via the carbonate-system solver - never sampled
baseline_chemistry_generation.domain_rule: Each Lee et al. (2006) zone equation has a published (T, S) validity domain; sampled (T, S) pairs outside the mapped equation's domain are rejected at the sampling stage and logged (validation rule V15)
baseline_chemistry_generation.coefficients_rule: All regression coefficients are transcribed from the source papers at implementation time and unit-tested against published example values - never typed from memory

archetypes.name: Polar / subpolar

expected_baseline_total_alkalinity_umol_.role: plausibility check on generated TA, not a sampling target

archetypes.ta_generation_method: Lee et al. (2006) high-latitude zone equation (Southern Ocean / North Pacific as appropriate to the draw)
archetypes.carbonate_constants_note: Rows with T < 2 C use the low-temperature-valid alternative constants set, recorded in the constants_set column (see equations_and_constants.json)
archetypes.notes: Low aragonite saturation state, high Revelle factor (low buffering capacity)

archetypes.name: Temperate

expected_baseline_total_alkalinity_umol_.role: plausibility check on generated TA, not a sampling target

archetypes.ta_generation_method: Lee et al. (2006) North Atlantic / North Pacific zone equation as appropriate to the draw

archetypes.name: Subtropical gyre

expected_baseline_total_alkalinity_umol_.role: plausibility check on generated TA, not a sampling target

archetypes.notes: High alkalinity, high aragonite saturation state

archetypes.name: Tropical

expected_baseline_total_alkalinity_umol_.role: plausibility check on generated TA, not a sampling target

archetypes.notes: Highest aragonite saturation state of the six archetypes

archetypes.name: Coastal, lower salinity

expected_baseline_total_alkalinity_umol_.role: plausibility check on generated TA, not a sampling target

archetypes.ta_generation_method: Two-end-member mixing line: regional open-ocean TA (from the mapped Lee et al. equation at the archetype's salinity ceiling) mixed toward a freshwater TA end-member, with a larger noise term. Lee et al. (2006) is an open-ocean product and is not applied directly here. Freshwater end-member range: SOURCE VERIFICATION REQUIRED
archetypes.notes: Greater natural variability represented by larger noise term; mixing-line assumption documented explicitly

archetypes.name: High-salinity marginal sea

expected_baseline_total_alkalinity_umol_.role: plausibility check on generated TA, not a sampling target

archetypes.ta_generation_method: Published Mediterranean-type TA-salinity relationship (candidate: Schneider et al. 2007; coefficients to be transcribed and verified at implementation). Lee et al. (2006) explicitly excludes marginal seas
archetypes.notes: Mediterranean-like conditions; not claimed to represent the Mediterranean Sea specifically

atmospheric_co2_ppm.note: Fixed in the core dataset (approx. mid-2020s level, NOAA GML); varied in sensitivity runs

baseline_disequilibrium_uatm.note: Represents natural seasonal/biological air-sea CO2 disequilibrium; pco2_0 = atmospheric_co2_ppm + disequilibrium

equilibration_fraction_f.type: kinetic/transport input parameter (uncertain), sampled per environment draw
equilibration_fraction_f.definition: Fraction of the way toward full air-sea equilibrium reached by the evaluation horizon (~1 year), limited by gas exchange, mixed-layer depth, and subduction. Scales realized uptake: realized = f x potential
equilibration_fraction_f.do_not_confuse_with: thermo_efficiency_eta_mol_mol (potential uptake / dose, ~0.75-0.85 mol CO2 per mol TA per literature) - that is a thermodynamic OUTPUT computed per row, never sampled. f and eta are different quantities and are never interchanged
equilibration_fraction_f.verification_note: The 0.55-0.95 range at a ~1-year horizon is provisional and flagged for verification against the regional equilibration results in He & Tyka (2023)
